2608.03616v1.feasibility_reason: The paper studies crypto-perpetual liquidation cascades using cross-asset correlation structure, branching ratios, and on-chain fill logs from multiple venues (Binance, Hyperliquid). We have only one futures instrument (NQ), no cross-sectional data, no liquidation mechanics, no multi-venue data, and no fill-level attribution. The core claim—measuring branching ratios and first-order transition signatures in a cascade—requires the multi-asset, multi-venue infrastructure that does not exist in our data.
2608.03616v1.title: Measuring the engine of a liquidation cascade: subcritical branching inside a first-order transition

2608.04373v3.claim: Persistent pseudonymous wallet addresses that reveal trader identity carry short-horizon price information that anonymous order-book data leave unmeasured, as evidenced by wallet-level markout persistence predicting one-second returns.
2608.04373v3.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires persistent wallet identity tracking across time to measure trader informativeness and predict returns. Our data is a single anonymous futures instrument with no wallet addresses, trader identifiers, or any mechanism to link orders across time to specific accounts. The core finding—that wallet-level markout persistence predicts returns—cannot be tested without the ability to identify and track individual traders.
2608.04373v3.title: Public Trader Identity: Adverse Selection and Return Predictability

2608.04832v1.claim: Policies trained under stationary ambiguity (where parameter uncertainty does not systematically decay over time) maintain robustness to latent regime shifts, whereas policies trained under vanishing ambiguity (static randomization) specialize to observed regimes and fail when parameters change.
2608.04832v1.feasibility_first_pass_reason: The paper's core claim—that policies trained under stationary ambiguity remain robust to latent regime shifts—can be tested on NQ futures hedging or directional control. The binding constraint is that we have only 384 train sessions (daily bars), which is tight for deep RL but sufficient for a proof-of-concept. The paper's hedging experiments are on derivatives; we can substitute a directional or volatility-targeting strategy on NQ futures instead.
2608.04832v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires testing hedging policies on simulated price paths with latent volatility regimes that shift over time. We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with 384 training sessions, making it impossible to construct the multi-asset hedging problems (straddles, worst-of calls, risk reversals on different underlyings) or to generate the controlled regime-shift scenarios the paper uses to evaluate 'continual robustness.' The paper's core contribution—that stationary ambiguity preserves robustness to latent parameter shifts—cannot be isolated on a single futures contract.
2608.04832v1.gate_reason: The paper's core contribution—that stationary ambiguity preserves robustness while decaying ambiguity causes specialization—is a claim about out-of-sample decay and what predicts it. This bears on how we measure and interpret robustness across regimes. However, the mechanism (RL policy learning under different simulator assumptions) is not directly comparable to our acceptance protocol, which is walk-forward validation on fixed feature sets.
2608.04832v1.protocol_edit: The paper suggests measuring whether a policy trained on one regime distribution remains robust when latent parameters shift. This could inform a gate check: does a strategy's performance degrade predictably when we test it on sessions with different volatility regimes or microstructure parameters? Add a regime-shift robustness measurement to the holdout evaluation, separate from walk-forward stability.
2608.04832v1.relevance_reason: The paper proposes a training procedure for RL policies in simulation, but the project has already falsified sequence models and deep networks at current sample size, and explicitly defers reinforcement learning pending resolution of reward-shaping questions. The adapted claim requires training a policy end-to-end, which is a project (machinery we do not have calibrated), not a campaign actionable on Tuesday.
2608.04832v1.speaks_to_deferral: auction-market-features (defers RL and deep networks), but the deferral is structural, not a question to resolve first.
2608.04832v1.title: Robust Control under Stationary Ambiguity

2608.05373v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires options market data (option prices, implied volatility, Delta, Greeks) and enforcement-labeled manipulation dates from two jurisdictions (Indian BANKNIFTY index options and U.S. equities from SEC v. Patel). We have only NQ futures tick data with no options chain, no Greeks, and no enforcement labels. The signature detection method is fundamentally built on option-state dynamics that do not exist in our data.
2608.05373v1.title: Velocity- and Regime-Aware Detection of Intraday Options Market Manipulation, with Explainable Attribution

2608.05755v2.claim: Learnable sector embeddings in LSTM networks improve directional return prediction by capturing industry momentum, a cross-sectional phenomenon requiring multiple stocks across different sectors.
2608.05755v2.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires a cross-section of S&P 500 stocks (500 constituents) to test sector embeddings and industry momentum effects. We have only one instrument (NQ futures), making cross-sectional heterogeneity and sector-level analysis impossible. The claim fundamentally depends on multiple assets with sector classifications.
2608.05755v2.title: Cross-Sectional Heterogeneity in LSTM Networks for Financial Time Series

2608.06048v1.claim: Given name frequency distributions in the USA and France follow Rayleigh-Jeans thermalization and condensation, producing stable Lorenz and Pareto curves with Gini coefficients between 0.85–0.95 over 100+ years.
2608.06048v1.feasibility_reason: This paper analyzes statistical distributions of baby names from government databases using Lorenz curves, Pareto distributions, and Rayleigh-Jeans thermalization theory. It requires cross-sectional demographic data (name frequencies across populations over time), not financial time series. The claim is entirely about social/demographic statistics and has no connection to trading, market microstructure, or price dynamics.
2608.06048v1.title: Thermodynamic statistics of given names in USA and France

2608.06618v1.claim: Joint factor-graph learning that redefines graph locality through factor exposures rather than co-movement produces portfolios that outperform correlation-based allocation across market regimes.
2608.06618v1.feasibility_reason: The paper requires a cross-section of 300 equities (S&P 500, Nikkei 225, STOXX 600 constituents) to learn joint factor-graph representations and test portfolio diversification. We have only one instrument (NQ futures), making cross-sectional analysis impossible. Additionally, the claim depends on comparing graph-based clustering against economic sectors (GICS), which requires multiple assets with sector labels—not applicable to a single futures contract.
2608.06618v1.title: Beyond Co-Movement: Locality by Exposures Enables a Joint Factor-Graph Framework for Portfolio Diversification

2608.07690v1.claim: Order imbalance in customer arrivals is absorbed exactly by a translation of the market maker's skew, a widening of quotes, and a multiplication of carrying cost, with the adjustment determined by the observable market width and the log-odds of arrival direction.
2608.07690v1.feasibility_reason: The paper is a theoretical market-making model for OTC dealer markets with sealed-bid auctions. It requires order-flow direction (buy/sell imbalance), competing quotes, and win rates—none of which exist in our data. NQ futures are continuous electronic limit-order markets, not OTC request-for-quote mechanisms, and we have no competing dealer quotes or win/loss outcomes on submitted bids.
2608.07690v1.title: On a Simple Relationship Between Order Imbalance, Skew and Width in Over-The-Counter Trading

2608.07709v1.claim: A Poisson-embedded marked Hawkes order-flow model with ordinary arrivals and rare marked arrivals converges in distribution to the rough Hawkes–Heston stochastic volatility model under near-critical scaling.
2608.07709v1.feasibility_reason: This paper is a pure mathematical finance theory paper proving convergence of a microscopic marked Hawkes order-flow model to a rough Hawkes–Heston stochastic volatility limit. It requires order-level data (marked Hawkes point processes with event classifications, marks, and intensities) and makes no empirical claims testable on price/volume data alone. The paper contains no backtests, no strategy, no performance metrics on real data—only convergence proofs and numerical illustrations of the theoretical limit.
2608.07709v1.title: Microstructural Foundation for the Rough Hawkes--Heston Model

2608.08625v1.claim: Partial retention of hidden excess clipped by daily price limits generates same-sign next-day mean returns and persistence probabilities that scale with band width.
2608.08625v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires daily price-limit circuit breaker events as the triggering mechanism. NQ futures have no daily price limits (they trade continuously with only intraday circuit breakers that do not clip returns). Without limit-close events, the core latent-state model cannot be tested.
2608.08625v1.title: Retained hidden excess generates memory in price-limited markets

2608.08825v1.claim: Hybrid neural-classical correction (combining frozen TimesFM with attention or bilinear neural modules plus Random Forest residual learning) achieves superior intraday return prediction on equities compared to frozen foundation models alone, with classical residual learning providing the largest single-component contribution.
2608.08825v1.feasibility_reason: The paper studies intraday return prediction on 10 individual equities (NVDA, MSFT, AAPL, etc.) using premarket signals. We have only one instrument (NQ futures), and the paper's central claim requires cross-sectional evaluation across multiple stocks to validate the hybrid neural-classical framework's generalization. A single futures contract cannot substitute for the equity cross-section the paper depends on.
2608.08825v1.title: Hybrid Neural-Classical Correction for Frozen Time Series Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Ablation Study on High-Frequency Stock Prediction

2608.09188v1.claim: Closed-window equity-perpetual marks are observationally equivalent across infinitely many oracle topologies (external anchoring vs. self/peer-reference networks) unless venues disclose their adjustment rules and support restrictions, which can be tested only against cash-market reopens that break the equivalence class.
2608.09188v1.feasibility_reason: The paper studies crypto equity-perpetual oracle mark formation during cash-market closures, requiring cross-venue oracle data, disclosed venue rules, and cash-market reopens for validation. We have only one futures instrument (NQ) with no access to crypto perpetual marks, venue oracle rules, or the cross-venue network structure the paper's entire identification strategy depends on.
2608.09188v1.title: When Cross-Venue Agreement Is Not Price Discovery: Disclosure Frontiers for 24/7 Equity-Perpetual Oracles

2608.09378v1.claim: Stablecoin transaction value distributions on Ethereum exhibit two distinct power-law scaling regimes: EOA-involved transactions cluster around exponent 1.45–1.60, while SC-SC transactions exhibit higher exponents of 1.72–1.73, with this separation robust across periods and stablecoins.
2608.09378v1.feasibility_reason: This paper analyzes blockchain transaction data (USDT/USDC on Ethereum) to estimate power-law exponents in stablecoin transfer value distributions. We have only NQ futures tick data with no blockchain, token, or cross-asset information. The paper's core claim—that transaction value distributions exhibit interaction-specific scaling regimes depending on whether transfers involve EOAs or smart contracts—requires blockchain transaction-level data that we do not possess.
2608.09378v1.title: Scaling laws of Stablecoin Transactions: Evidence from USDT and USDC on the Ethereum blockchain

2608.09641v1.claim: The smallest eigenvalues of financial correlation matrices contain information about market synchronization and effective dimensionality reduction, with predictive power for systemic risk that exceeds upper-spectrum indicators.
2608.09641v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires a cross-sectional correlation matrix of multiple assets to compute eigenvalue spectra and apply Random Matrix Theory. We have only one instrument (NQ futures), so no correlation structure exists. The methodology fundamentally depends on analyzing how eigenvalues of an N×N correlation matrix behave across assets—this requires N > 1 assets observed simultaneously.
2608.09641v1.title: Lower spectrum of financial correlation matrices: a new perspective on market synchronization

2608.10693v1.claim: Machine learning models (ConvLSTM) can forecast the implied volatility surface of S&P 500 index options and capture pre-FOMC announcement effects better than a random walk benchmark.
2608.10693v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires an implied volatility surface constructed from options on S&P 500 index. We have only NQ futures tick data with no options, no quotes, no bid/ask, and no option prices. An IV surface cannot be constructed from futures alone.
2608.10693v1.title: When the Fed Speaks: Dynamics and Forecasts of the Volatility Surface

2608.10788v1.claim: The Triadic Stress Index, built from closed triangles and network properties of asset correlation matrices, detects systemic financial stress as well as or better than spectral baselines like the Absorption Ratio, while providing parameter-free per-asset attribution of stress concentration.
2608.10788v1.feasibility_reason: The paper tests a network-based systemic stress index on correlation matrices of multiple asset classes (equities, crypto, commodities, FX, sovereign debt) across 20-year histories with dozens to hundreds of assets per test. We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with 384 training sessions, making cross-sectional correlation networks impossible and the sample size far too small for the paper's methodology.
2608.10788v1.title: The Triadic Stress Index in Financial Markets

This becomes a single-instrument characterization study rather than a crypto–equity comparison. The claim shifts from 'cryptocurrencies differ from equities' to 'NQ exhibits these specific ordinal and visibility signatures.' The paper's comparative structure and its conclusion about asset-class heterogeneity cannot be preserved.
2608.10852v2.claim: Cryptocurrencies and equity-index futures share heavy-tailed distributions and volatility clustering but differ in local ordinal organization (weaker for crypto) and high-degree visibility asymmetry (larger for crypto), detectable via CECP and DHVG diagnostics at one-minute resolution.
2608.10852v2.feasibility_reason: The paper's core claim—that cryptocurrencies and equity futures share macroscopic stylized facts but differ in ordinal structure and time-directed visibility—can be tested on NQ futures tick data. However, the paper compares three cryptocurrencies against one equity benchmark (S&P 500 futures). We have only NQ futures, eliminating the cross-asset comparison that is central to the paper's design.
2608.10852v2.gate_reason: The paper offers no acceptance protocol, null construction, multiple-testing correction, or measurement of out-of-sample decay. Its diagnostics (CECP, DHVG) are applied post-hoc to characterize data, not to evaluate a predictive claim or establish significance thresholds. It does not bear on how we judge a result.
2608.10852v2.relevance_reason: The paper characterizes statistical properties of price series (ordinal organization, visibility-graph structure) but proposes no mechanism a strategy could act on and no condition under which an edge would appear. Even after Stage 1's adaptation to single-instrument characterization, it remains a descriptive study of market microstructure with no actionable claim.
2608.10852v2.title: Universality and Heterogeneity of Stylized Facts in Cryptocurrency and Equity Markets

2608.11250v1.claim: An autonomous alpha-discovery system combining LLM proposal, adversarial verification, and pending-aware budget allocation can produce platform-validated trading factors with Fitness and Sharpe metrics comparable to or exceeding published benchmarks.
2608.11250v1.feasibility_reason: AgonAlpha discovers cross-sectional equity alphas on WorldQuant BRAIN using fundamental, technical, and options data across a broad universe (U.S. TOP3000). The paper's central claim—that an LLM-driven system can autonomously discover and verify trading factors—requires the ability to test factors across many securities and data types that we do not have.
2608.11250v1.title: AgonAlpha: Autonomous Alpha Discovery via Prompt Economy and Scalable Agentic Search

2608.11327v1.claim: A transformer trained on sparse sets of (account, quarter, value) tuples outperforms classical ML, chained gradient boosting, LLMs, and foundation models at forecasting complete financial statements 1–20 quarters ahead.
2608.11327v1.feasibility_reason: The paper forecasts complete financial statements (78 accounting line items) 1–20 quarters ahead using quarterly Compustat data. We have only one futures instrument (NQ) with tick-level trade data, no financial statements, no accounting items, and no fundamental data whatsoever. The paper's entire task—predicting balance sheets, income statements, and cash flows—is structurally impossible on intraday futures prices.
2608.11327v1.title: Long-Horizon Forecasting of Complete Financial Statements with Forma

We have only one instrument (NQ futures), no betting market data, no match outcomes, and no cross-sectional structure analogous to independent matches.
2608.11505v1.title: Does a Structural Model Add Anything to the Closing Price? Calibrated forecasting, incremental information, and match leverage in the Italian Serie A

2608.12251v1.claim: A regime-gated residual mixture-of-experts architecture improves cross-sectional volatility forecasting by using regime variables only for expert routing rather than as direct forecasting inputs.
2608.12251v1.feasibility_reason: The paper studies cross-sectional volatility forecasting across 1,027 U.S. equities and 1,552 Japanese equities. We have only one instrument (NQ futures), so we cannot construct a cross-section. The entire experimental design—pooling stock-level features, computing cross-sectional correlations (IC), and evaluating on 1.9 million stock-day forecasts—requires multiple assets. A single futures contract has no cross-section.
2608.12251v1.title: Regime-Gated Residual Mixture-of-Experts for Cross-Sectional Volatility Forecasting

2608.12259v1.claim: Activation calibration strategy (abs-max vs. percentile) is a first-order determinant of 4-bit post-training quantization performance in financial time-series forecasting, with percentile calibration recovering 53–94% of degradation in affected architectures.
2608.12259v1.feasibility_reason: The paper studies cross-sectional volatility forecasting on S&P 500 equities (501 stocks, daily bars, 2.1M asset-days). We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with no cross-section, no equity constituents, and no ability to construct the cross-sectional ranking task that is central to the claim. The paper's metric (daily information coefficient from cross-sectional Spearman correlation) requires multiple assets ranked on the same date.
2608.12259v1.title: Calibration Bets on the Past: Post-Training Quantization for Financial Time-Series Forecasting

2608.12424v2.claim: A Bayesian vector autoregression model integrating topic analysis, sentiment analysis, and macroeconomic variables can forecast interest rate swap curves more accurately than traditional econometric models, improving strategic asset-liability management in banks.
2608.12424v2.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim is that an AI-driven multiscenario interest rate forecasting system improves banking ALM and risk management. Our data is intraday NQ futures tick data with no macroeconomic variables, no interest rates, no cross-asset data, and no monthly aggregation capability that would preserve the economic relationships the paper models.
2608.12424v2.title: AI-Driven Multiscenario Interest Rate Forecasting: A Proof of Concept for Banking Asset Management

2608.12493v1.claim: Implied variance surfaces evolve under spot movements according to a transport velocity field whose jets govern level, skew, and curvature dynamics, and this field can be nonparametrically identified from market data and tested against classical stickiness regimes.
2608.12493v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires a cross-sectional implied volatility surface (multiple strikes and maturities) to estimate transport coefficients and test smile dynamics. We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with no options data, no implied volatility surface, and no quotes or order-book depth. The empirical work (Section 8) uses five years of SPX implied-volatility snapshots across seven tenors and eleven moneyness levels—data we cannot construct from futures tick data.
2608.12493v1.title: Beyond the Skew-Stickiness Ratio: Transport Geometry of Spot-Driven Variance Surface Dynamics

2608.12583v1.feasibility_reason: This is a survey paper reviewing diffusion-model applications across financial data types (time series, limit order books, tabular data, structured objects). Testing it would require implementing dozens of distinct models on different data modalities, which is outside the scope of validating a single claim.
2608.12583v1.title: Diffusion Models in Finance: A Survey

Our data is a single futures instrument (NQ) with intraday tick-level trade data, containing no company fundamentals, no cross-section, and no valuation targets. The paper's supervised similarity learning framework is fundamentally incompatible with univariate time-series futures data.
2608.12594v1.title: What Makes a Peer? Valuation-Anchored Similarity in Private Markets

2608.12634v1.claim: Official Shariah-compliant classification changes alter the feasible investor base sufficiently to produce measurable price effects when the affected security is sufficiently tradable, but formal eligibility alone is insufficient without institutional recognition and marginal constrained demand.
2608.12634v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires a cross-section of equities with heterogeneous Shariah-screening classifications and official list events. The mechanism—institutional rules determining who may own a security and how classification changes affect segmented investor bases—is entirely absent from futures markets.
2608.12634v1.title: The Price of Permission: Classification Uncertainty in Constrained Capital Markets

2608.13082v1.claim: An embedding-based metric (LOB-ID) using DeepLOB Inception features can evaluate synthetic limit order book data by detecting joint temporal and cross-level structure that statistic-based and moment-matching approaches miss.

2608.13082v1.title: LOB-ID: Evaluating Synthetic Market Data by Inception Distances

2608.13096v1.claim: Flow-matching models can generate realistic multi-level limit order book continuations more efficiently than diffusion models while maintaining controllability over market regimes (trend, volatility, liquidity, imbalance).
2608.13096v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim is that a flow-matching generative model can produce realistic limit order book (LOB) trajectories with controllable scenario generation. This requires order book depth data (ten price levels per side with prices and volumes), which we do not have. We only have tick-level trade data with aggressor side, not the full LOB state at each timestamp.
2608.13096v1.title: FlowLOB: Efficient and Controllable Limit Order Book Generation with Flow Matching

The paper derives theoretical algorithms and demonstrates them on synthetic examples (Bessel, CEV, Feller processes) with known closed-form solutions or controlled parameters—not market data.
2608.13732v2.title: On the First Hitting Time Problems for Diffusion Processes: Local Time-Space Approach

2608.14014v1.claim: News-aligned price moves concentrate before and at publication for most event types, with markets underreacting to quantified fundamental news and overreacting to soft narrative news, as measured by beta-adjusted abnormal returns across thousands of stock-day events.
2608.14014v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires a cross-sectional study of ~3,000 US stocks with daily news events and returns measured across a large sample (1.68M events, 384 trading days). The paper's findings depend on comparing how different stocks and news types react to events—a comparison that requires multiple securities.
2608.14014v1.title: Buy the Rumor, Sell the News: When Is News Priced In?

2608.14323v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires a cross-section of firm characteristics (94 characteristics per stock) to estimate dependence structure and predict relative returns across many stocks. We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with no firm-level data, characteristics, or cross-sectional dimension. The method is fundamentally designed for equity cross-sections, not single-instrument time series.
2608.14323v1.title: Dependence-Informed Sparse Neural Architecture for Stock Return Prediction

2608.14859v1.claim: Disclosed human-capital disruption in earnings calls predicts firm-specific idiosyncratic volatility, downside risk, and executive turnover within firms over time.
2608.14859v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires cross-sectional equity data (13,201 firm-years across 2,870 firms with earnings calls, accounting data, and executive rosters). We have only one futures instrument (NQ) with 384 training sessions, making cross-sectional analysis and firm-level variation impossible. The paper measures firm-specific risk and organizational outcomes; neither construct applies to a single commodity futures contract.
2608.14859v1.title: Disclosed Human-Capital Disruption and Firm-Specific Risk

2608.15597v1.title: Toward Decentralized Carbon Trading in Indonesia: A Public-Blockchain Architecture for Tokenized Real-World Assets

The claim concerns blockchain economics, not price prediction or trading.
2608.15640v1.title: A contribution to the critique of blockchain censorship

The method requires learning separate auxiliary tasks and policies across multiple assets and regimes; this is a fundamentally different problem from single-instrument intraday trading on NQ futures.
2608.15841v1.title: Self-Supervised Auxiliary Task Discovery for Stable Reinforcement Learning in Stock Trading

2608.17636v1.feasibility_reason: This paper is a numerical methods paper for multi-asset European option pricing under characteristic-function models. It requires access to joint characteristic functions of multiple assets and prices multi-asset derivatives (baskets, min/max options). We have only one instrument (NQ futures), no cross-sectional data, no options market, and no ability to construct multi-asset characteristic functions.
2608.17636v1.title: COS-TT-CHF: A Tensor-Train Characteristic-Function COS Method for Multi-Asset Option Pricing

2608.17808v3.title: Self-Consistent Adjoint Policy Iteration for Constrained Dynamic Portfolio Choice

2608.18195v1.claim: A reinforcement learning algorithm using logistic-normal distributions and deep-set encoders can learn to maximize market-making revenue by dynamically placing limit orders across multiple price levels while managing inventory, outperforming fixed heuristic benchmarks in simulated limit-order-book environments with noise, tactical, and strategic traders.
2608.18195v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires testing a market-making RL algorithm in a simulated limit order book with multi-level order placement, queue positions, and adaptive responses to order-book state. We have only tick-level NQ futures data with aggressor side, no order-book depth, no queue positions, no ability to inject fills or simulate counterparty responses. 2609.03552v1.title: An Entropic Factor Model for Robust Portfolio Replication

2609.04087v1.title: Global Multi-Maturity SPX-VIX Calibration Beyond Markovian Stitching

2609.04420v1.title: Optimal Stratified Allocation for Rare-Event Onset Forecasting in Dependent Sequences

2609.05491v1.title: Asymptotically-informed neural networks for Black-Scholes implied volatility computation

Daily bars (384 sessions) are infeasible for the statistical power needed to estimate and validate the nonlinear parametric model and its Shapley decomposition.

We have NQ futures tick data with buy/sell volume, which is structurally similar. However, the paper uses 10 stocks (5 large-tick, 5 small-tick) from June 2024 with ~50% train/test split, yielding roughly 200k+ intraday observations per stock. Our constraint is 384 training sessions (daily bars), which is ~1,800× fewer observations. The claim is testable on intraday NQ bars, but not on daily bars—sample size is the binding constraint.
2609.06085v1.gate_reason: The paper offers no acceptance protocol, null construction, overfitting correction, or measurement of out-of-sample decay that would change how we judge a result. Its contribution is a mechanism (nonlinear saturation) and a method (Shapley decomposition) to extract it; neither bears on the gate's error rates, thresholds, or falsified-families list.
2609.06085v1.hypothesis_edit: Add to intraday-continuation: split the continuation/reversal prediction by lagged-return sign and magnitude; test whether nonlinear (saturating) signed-volume impact outperforms linear volume in predicting next-bar direction.
2609.06085v1.relevance_reason: The paper's separable claim—that lagged signed volume generates nonlinear, saturating price-impact effects and that lagged returns act as state variables conditioning flow persistence—is testable on intraday NQ and could refine the continuation/reversal question. However, it does not directly address an open hypothesis; it would add a state-conditioning mechanism to questions already closed (intraday-continuation rejected 6 times), and the mechanism itself (nonlinear saturation in volume impact) was not the binding constraint in those rejections.
2609.06085v1.speaks_to_deferral: None. The paper does not address a deferred question (regime models, RL, deep networks). It proposes a mechanism for a closed question.
2609.06085v1.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Price-Trade Dynamics: From Black-Box Forecasts to Effective Parametric Models

Our data is a single futures contract with only trade-level tick data; we have no ability to define, price, or compute Greeks for any derivative payoff structure, nor do we have the pricing models (GBM, Heston, Hull-White) or AAD infrastructure the paper depends on.
2609.06137v1.title: Unbiased Monte Carlo Greeks for Discontinuous Payoffs

2609.07207v1.relevance_reason: The paper proposes a measurement technique (robust filtering for volatility estimation) with no edge to trade on. 2609.07207v1.title: Filtering without recursion and some of its uses in financial economics
